findings.title: The recommended public checkpointed-build handoff cannot resolve browser-game's required private standards

artifact: research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:47 recommends that playable-increment making reuse the public checkpointed-build workflow.

research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:49 requires every making call to name its applicable package-private standard and correctly notes that a call to public checkpointed-build opens that workflow's own package scope.
research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:255 requires literal names to resolve under the updated package rules.
owners: custom-workflow-authoring.md, Workflow packages: a public top-level workflow starts its own package scope; a private helper keeps the enclosing public scope.
custom-workflow-authoring.md: a path, dictionary, or private name cannot grant package scope.
installed tickets_frame.py::_workflow_record: a public workflow starts its own package scope and returns that public owner as inherited workflow context.
installed tickets_mint.py::_cmd_do_or_judge: child do/judge calls resolve standards with owner=workflow_context['workflow'].
skills/workflows/checkpointed-build/SKILL.md: its standard and narrowing names are consumed by do/judge calls parented to its own frame.
evidence.consequence: Inside checkpointed-build, browser-game-code, browser-game-visual, and browser-game-playtest are looked up under checkpointed-build's package rather than browser-game's. They are private to browser-game and therefore do not resolve. Passing a path or caller-owner dictionary is intentionally not a supported escape.

Quote the shared bounded-repair and outside-close idioms there. Only move a browser-game standard to a public ring if it has independently justified callers and ownership.

findings.title: The 60 fps hard gate measures callback cadence but leaves presented-frame failures without a rejecting threshold

artifact: research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:187 makes metric and threshold part of each performance cell.
research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:189 defines hard thresholds only for requestAnimationFrame callback rate/intervals and unexplained stalls.

research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:191 requires a Chrome trace to record dropped and partially presented frames but calls it corroboration and states no pass/fail threshold or contradiction rule.
research/browser-game-workflow-spec-2026-09-05.md:201 passes on every declared performance cell, so the callback-only thresholds can remain green despite adverse trace evidence.

primary_source.observation: Chrome documents green frames as rendered in time, partially presented frames as only some visual updates arriving in time, and dropped frames as not rendered in reasonable time.

evidence.consequence: A GPU/compositor-bound game can keep main-thread requestAnimationFrame callbacks near 60 Hz while missing visual presentation deadlines. The specified cell can therefore pass while the game does not deliver the declared frame rate.

findings.why_blocking: The frozen Goal requires a valid declared-hardware 60 fps target. The present hard gate can accept a false 60 fps claim at the fixed specification identity.
findings.smallest_change: Add an explicit presented-frame metric and threshold from the browser trace (including how partial and dropped frames are counted), and state that a callback/trace contradiction fails the cell until attributed and resolved. Bind that result into the outside evidence-index probe.

causes.cause: The design treats a reusable public workflow as though it can consume package-private identities from its caller after package ownership has intentionally changed.
causes.repair_scope: Specification document only. No runtime or resolver change is warranted.

causes.cause: The performance contract equates the scheduling cadence visible to requestAnimationFrame with delivered visual-frame cadence, while leaving the independent presentation trace qualitative.
